questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one word substitute for the underlined group of words in the given sentence.

In the world of espionage, the agent's ability to remain unnoticed and blend seamlessly into different environments was truly extraordinary.
questions.solution:
Ubiquitous: Present, appearing, or found everywhere; widespread.

Pretension: The assertion of a claim to a right; a false or ambitious claim.

Inconspicuous: Not easily noticeable or attracting attention; not conspicuous.

Redundant: Not or no longer needed or useful; superfluous.

Among the given options, 'inconspicuous' can be used as a one word substitute for the underlined group of words in the sentence.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.question:
Choose the word from the options that is Opposite in meaning to the given word.

Indigenous
questions.solution: 'Indigenous' means '(Adj)Originating or occurring naturally in a particular place'. Options b) and c) can be rejected as they are unrelated to the word. 'Native' means 'A person born in a specified place or associated with a place by birth, whether subsequently resident there or not.'. Hence, option a) can also be rejected as it is the same meaning as the word. 'Cogent' means '(of an argument or case) clear, logical, and convincing.'. 'Scintillating' means 'Sparkling or shining brightly.'. Hence, option d) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the sentence that has no spelling errors.

options.label: A
options.text: I was basicaly told to keep off your back, but no one mentioned I should run errands for you.

options.label: B
options.text: Destiny is a mysterious force that none can compreehend.

options.label: C
options.text: I can't believe that it's healthey to push them from your mind altogether.

options.label: D
options.text: He pushed the passenger's side door open, and she leaned down to look at him.

questions.solution:
Option (a)- The incorrectly spelt word is 'basicaly' and 'basically' is the correct word.

Option (b)- The incorrectly spelt word is 'compreehend' and 'comprehend' is the correct word. 'Comprehend' means 'to understand something completely'.

Option (c)- The incorrectly spelt word is 'healthey' and 'healthy' is the correct word.

So, only option (d) has no spelling errors.

Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The lecturer spoke so quietly that he was scarcely _______ at the back of the hall.
questions.solution:
The sentence conveys that the lecturer spoke very quietly, so it is obvious that his voice might not be able to reach the back of the hall. Thus, 'audible (able to be heard)' is the correct choice for the blank. Since an adjective would fit in the blank to describe the way he spoke, the adverb 'necessarily' is eliminated. The rest of the options do not fit well in the given context.

'Credible' means able to be believed; convincing.

Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate SYNONYM to replace the underlined word.

As a teacher, it's important to impart not only knowledge but also values to the students.
questions.solution:
"Impart" means to transmit or pass on (information, knowledge, or something abstract) to someone. 'Convey' means to communicate or pass on information, knowledge, or values to someone. So, the two words can be used as synonyms of each other. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

Withhold: To refuse to give or share something; to keep something back.

Retain: To keep or hold onto something; to continue to have possession or control of it.

Suppress: To forcibly put an end to something; to prevent the expression or development of something.

questions.question:
Choose the word from the options that is most similar in meaning to the given word.

Heedless
questions.solution: 'Heedless' means '(Adj) Showing a reckless lack of care or attention'. Options a) and d) can be rejected as they are unrelated to the word. 'Alert' means 'Quick to notice any unusual and potentially dangerous or difficult circumstances; vigilant.'. Hence, option c) can also be rejected as it is the exact opposite. 'Avow' means 'Assert or confess openly.'. 'Tantamount' means 'Equivalent in seriousness to; virtually the same as.'. Hence, option b) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Choose the sentence that uses a homonym of the underlined word:

The bat flew silently across the dark cave.

options.label: A
options.text: He swung the bat and hit the ball out of the ground.

options.label: B
options.text: The bat hung upside down inside the cave.

options.label: C
options.text: A small bat emerged from the hollow tree.

options.label: D
options.text: The bat spread its wings and disappeared into the night.

questions.solution:
In the question, "bat" refers to a flying mammal.

A homonym is a word that has the same spelling or pronunciation but a different meaning.

Option (a) uses "bat" to mean a piece of sports equipment used in games such as cricket or baseball, which is a different meaning.

Options (b), (c), and (d) all refer to the animal, which is the same meaning as the sentence in the question.

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question: The word "fluctuations" as used in the passage most nearly means:
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the passage and answer the questions:

In the ever expanding age of digital connectivity, both Wi-Fi and Air Fibre have emerged as prominent solutions for delivering internet access to homes and businesses. Wi-Fi typically refers to a wireless network created through a broadband connection such as fibre or cable, allowing multiple devices within a limited area to connect to the internet without physical cables. Air Fibre, on the other hand, delivers broadband through radio signals transmitted between towers and receivers installed at the user's premises. The growing demand for high-speed internet has led many consumers to compare these technologies not only in terms of speed but also reliability, accessibility, and cost.

One of the main advantages of Wi-Fi connected through fibre broadband is stability. Since the primary data transmission occurs through underground or optical fibre cables, the connection is generally less affected by weather conditions or signal interference. Fibre-based networks are capable of providing extremely high speeds and consistent performance, making them suitable for activities such as streaming, online gaming, and remote work. However, the limitation lies in infrastructure availability. Fibre cables must be physically installed in a particular area, and in many remote or newly developed regions, this infrastructure may not yet exist.

Air Fibre attempts to overcome this limitation by using wireless transmission from nearby communication towers. Because it does not rely on extensive underground cabling, it can often be deployed more quickly and can bring internet access to areas where fibre installation would be expensive or slow. This makes it particularly useful in semi-urban or rural locations. Nevertheless, Air Fibre connections may sometimes experience fluctuations in speed due to environmental factors such as heavy rain, obstacles between towers, or network congestion. Ultimately, the comparison between Wi-Fi through fibre and Air Fibre reflects a trade-off between stability and flexibility. Fibre-based Wi-Fi offers highly reliable and consistent performance where infrastructure is available, while Air Fibre provides broader accessibility and faster deployment in underserved areas.

options.label: A
options.text: sudden improvements in internet service quality

options.label: C
options.text: irregular changes in speed or performance

questions.solution: The word appears in Paragraph 3 in the phrase "Air Fibre connections may sometimes experience fluctuations in speed." The context explains that environmental factors such as rain, obstacles, or network congestion may affect the connection. This indicates that the speed may change or vary at different times rather than remain constant. Therefore, "fluctuations" most nearly means irregular changes in speed or performance. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution:
Among the given options, (d) is the only one correctly spelt. The word means the condition, state, or quality of being free or as free as possible from all flaws or defects. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The correct spelling of option (a) is 'bizarre' (means 'very strange or unusual').

The correct spelling of option (b) is 'infatuation' (means 'feeling of foolish or obsessively strong love for, admiration for, or interest in someone or something').

The correct spelling of option (c) is 'fortunate' (means 'favoured by or involving good luck; lucky').

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

One who is eager or anxious to do something
questions.solution:
Vibrant: Full of energy and life.

Solicitous: One who is full of anxiety and concern.

Pragmatic: dealing with things sensibly and realistically in a way that is based on practical rather than theoretical considerations.

Soliloquy: an act of speaking one's thoughts aloud when by oneself or regardless of any hearers, especially by a character in a play.

B is the right answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, a statement has been given with highlighted text. Select the option that can replace the text with the correct idiom or phrase.

She was able to make progress in her career within a short span of time.
questions.solution:
The phrase 'make headway' means to make progress. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

Turn heads- if something or someone turns heads, people notice them because they look interesting or attractive.

Hit the headlines- to become important news and be reported in the newspapers and on the television and radio.

Heart sinks- to feel sad or worried.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

You lay yourself open to ______ by suggesting such an outlandish plan.
questions.solution:
A noun is required in the blank to show the response of the people after suggesting a weird plan. So, the adverb 'jokingly' is eliminated. 'Copy' does not fit well in the given context. Nobody would 'praise' the person for suggesting a weird plan. Thus, 'ridicule(mockery)' is the correct choice.

Complete sentence: You lay yourself open to ridicule by suggesting such an outlandish plan.

Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word.

The impending storm forced residents to prepare for the approaching weather with urgency.
questions.solution:
Impending: Something that is about to happen or is looming on the horizon.

Exhibiting: Displaying or presenting something for others to see or observe.

Transcendent: Going beyond ordinary limits; surpassing; exceeding.

Radiating: Emitting or sending out rays or waves; spreading out in all directions.

Averted: Turned away or aside; prevented or avoided.

Among the given options, the word 'averted' is opposite in meaning to the underlined word 'impending'. So, the two words can be used as antonyms of each other.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.source: SSC CGL Tier II Live Test: Oct 23-25
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct phrasal verb.

The editor asked the writer to ________ the unnecessary paragraphs from the article.
questions.solution:
a) "Cut down" means to reduce in quantity but is less suitable for removing specific paragraphs.

b) "Cut out" means to remove or eliminate something entirely, which fits the context best.

c) "Cut across" means to affect different groups or to take a shorter route.

d) " Cut through" means to pass through something or deal directly with a problem or confusion.

Therefore, the correct answer is (b) cut out.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate collocation to substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

Why do you think that you're cut in for this job?
questions.solution:
Collocation is the combination of words formed when two or more words are often used together in a way that sounds correct.

The correct collocation is "cut out for" which means "naturally able or suited to do or be (something)".

Other options are incorrect collocations.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Pivotal
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

Augmented Reality (AR) is revolutionising education by enhancing learning experiences through its ability to merge digital information with the real world. This innovative technology enables students to interact with virtual objects and environments overlaid on their physical surroundings, thereby transforming abstract concepts into tangible, immersive learning experiences. One of the primary benefits of AR in education is its capability to visualise complex information. Subjects that traditionally rely on textbooks and two-dimensional images, such as biology and chemistry, can now be taught using interactive 3D models. For example, students can dissect virtual organisms or manipulate molecular structures in real time, gaining a deeper understanding of spatial relationships and processes that are difficult to grasp through static illustrations alone. Moreover, AR promotes active learning by encouraging exploration and discovery. Instead of passively absorbing information, students engage with content in dynamic ways. Historical events can be recreated in AR, allowing learners to witness pivotal moments firsthand at historical sites or even in their classrooms. This contextualization not only makes history more vivid and memorable but also facilitates deeper connections between past events and present-day implications.

AR also enhances collaborative learning environments. Students can collaborate on projects where they design and interact with virtual simulations together. In fields like architecture and engineering, teams can prototype and visualise complex structures in real-world contexts, fostering teamwork, problem-solving skills, and creative thinking. Furthermore, AR supports personalised learning experiences by catering to individual learning styles and paces. Visual learners benefit from interactive visualisations, while auditory learners can receive audio instructions or explanations overlaid with physical objects. This adaptability helps educators tailor educational content to meet diverse student needs, promoting inclusivity and equity in the classroom.

Despite these advantages, integrating AR into education poses challenges such as cost, infrastructure requirements, and the need for teacher training. Schools must invest in suitable devices and software, ensure robust internet connectivity, and provide educators with adequate support and professional development opportunities to effectively integrate AR into their teaching practices.
questions.solution: "Pivotal" means of crucial importance, central, or critical to the outcome or success of something. Among the given options, "crucial" best captures the meaning of "pivotal" as it denotes something that is extremely important or essential. 'Trivial' refers to something that is of little importance or significance; insignificant. 'Minor' refers to something that is of lesser importance or significance; not major or significant. 'Alternate' means reciprocal or mutual. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, choose the word opposite in meaning to the given word.

Surly
questions.solution: Surly/ gruff - unfriendly and bad-tempered. Coarse - rough. Inane - lacking sense. Amiable - friendly and good-natured. D is the right answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate collocation to substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

They were all amazed of my knowledge and skill.
questions.solution:
Collocation is the combination of words formed when two or more words are often used together in a way that sounds correct.

The correct collocation is "amazed by" which means "feeling or showing great surprise or wonder".

Other options are incorrect collocations.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

To ace this quiz competition, we must keep our fingers on the pulse as regards technology.

options.label: A
options.text: Put up a plan or idea into action

options.label: C
options.text: Be constantly aware of the most recent developments

options.label: D
options.text: Be serious about what you announce

questions.solution: 'Keep your fingers on the pulse' refers to being constantly aware of recent developments. Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Instigate or stir up
questions.solution: Foment - Instigate or stir up (an undesirable or violent sentiment or course of action). Dehort - Strongly dissuade (someone) from a course of action. Discord - Disagreement between people. Corroborate - Confirm or give support to (a statement, theory, or finding). Option C is the right answer.

questions.question: The word "resonate" in the passage most nearly means:
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the passage and answer the questions:

Living far from one's native place or country often brings with it a quiet but persistent discomfort, most noticeably in the aspect of food. Meals are not merely a means of sustenance; they are deeply tied to memory, culture, and a sense of belonging. When individuals move away from home, they may find themselves surrounded by unfamiliar cuisines, different cooking styles, and altered flavours that fail to resonate with what they have grown up eating. Even when alternatives are available, they rarely replicate the authenticity of home-cooked meals. Over time, this gap between familiarity and availability begins to weigh heavily, turning everyday eating into a reminder of distance rather than comfort.

The absence of one's go-to meal or comfort food can have a surprisingly profound emotional impact. A simple dish, often taken for granted back home, carries with it the warmth of family, tradition, and routine. When that dish becomes inaccessible or is only poorly imitated, it leaves a sense of incompleteness. One may attempt to recreate it, but the difference in ingredients, water, or even cooking conditions often alters the taste. As a result, the experience feels inadequate, almost like a memory that cannot be fully relived. In such moments, food ceases to satisfy the soul, even if it fills the stomach.

Moreover, this culinary disconnect gradually intensifies the feeling of displacement. Social gatherings, festivals, and even daily routines are closely associated with specific foods, and their absence can make one feel detached from their own cultural identity. While people eventually adapt to new cuisines, the longing for familiar tastes never truly disappears. It lingers in small cravings, in comparisons, and in the constant search for something that feels "just right." In this sense, living away from home is not just a geographical shift but an emotional one, where the lack of familiar food becomes a subtle yet powerful reminder of what has been left behind.
questions.solution: The passage mentions "flavours that fail to resonate with what they have grown up eating." (Paragraph 1). Here, "resonate" implies forming a meaningful connection or sense of familiarity with past experiences. Among the options, "connect" best captures this contextual meaning. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the sentence that uses the given idiom correctly.

Bite off more than you can chew

options.label: A
options.text: She bit off more than she could chew when she decided to run a marathon without any training.

options.label: B
options.text: The manager always bites off more than he can chew when he orders food at a restaurant.

options.label: C
options.text: I like to bite off more than I can chew when I study for exams because it motivates me to work harder.

options.label: D
options.text: They bit off more than they could chew when they refused to buy the house for which they couldn't afford the mortgage.

questions.solution:
The idiom "bite off more than you can chew" means to take on a task that is too difficult or demanding for one's abilities or resources. It usually has a negative connotation. Option (a) uses the idiom correctly, as it implies that she took on a challenge that was beyond her capacity and likely failed or suffered. The other options either use the idiom in a positive or neutral way or in a literal sense, which is not appropriate.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the sentence which has no spelling error.

options.label: A
options.text: They've just built some hidous new apartment blocks on the seafront.

options.label: B
options.text: She wears the most hideous colour combinations you could ever imagine.

options.label: C
options.text: The bathroom was pink and green and silver  -  it was absolutely hideuous.

options.label: D
options.text: Their crime is discovered by a piece of hideuos bad luck.

questions.solution:
The sentence in option (b) has no error.

All other sentences have the word 'hideous' incorrectly spelt.

'Hideous' means 'extremely ugly'.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.question:
Select the right phrasal verb for the blank.

We decided to ____ our old tile-roofed building as it was withering too much.
questions.solution:
Pull over- To slow down and move to the side of the road

Pull up- Come to a halt

Pull down- Demolish a building

Pull in- Move to the side of or off the road

The sentence talks about the decision to do something about an old, roofed building. Among the options, 'pull over', 'pull up' and 'pull in' are contextually irrelevant and so they are negated. 'Pull down' matches the context of the sentence and describes what is decided about the building and is also grammatically correct.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Note:

Phrasal verb: A phrase that consists of a verb with a preposition or adverb or both, the meaning of which is different from the meaning of its separate parts. Example: She has always looked down on me. Here, the phrasal verb 'to look down on someone' doesn't mean that you are looking down from a higher place at someone who is below you; it means that you think that you are better than someone.

questions.question:
Choose the sentence that uses a homonym of the underlined word:

She stood at the foot of the mountain, gazing upward.

options.label: A
options.text: He injured his foot while playing soccer.

options.label: B
options.text: The foot of the bed was decorated with a colorful quilt.

options.label: C
options.text: The hikers rested at the foot of the hill.

options.label: D
options.text: The foot of the couch had carved wooden legs.

questions.solution:
Homonyms are words that are spelled the same and pronounced the same but have different meanings. In the original sentence, "foot" is a noun meaning the base or bottom part of a mountain. Options b), c) and d) use "foot" in the sense of a base of a natural feature or to refer to the end or bottom part of furniture, which is similar to the original sense. Among these, option a) is the intended homonym, using "foot" as a body part.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.
